strengths: The task is practically relevant: automatic category discovery removes the need for users to specify a segmentation vocabulary. Decoding clustered subsets of BLIP patch embeddings is a useful technical idea that integrates with existing segmenters without additional weight training.

Table 1 provides consistent evidence that local captioning improves class-agnostic segmentation over BLIP plus X-Decoder: cmIoU increases from 38.0 to 41.9 on VOC, 26.7 to 29.2 on ADE20K, and 29.2 to 35.8 on Cityscapes.

The pipeline is understandable, and the manuscript supplies substantial hyperparameter details and evaluator pseudocode. Appendix B usefully documents hallucinated nouns, overly generic labels, and competition between related categories.
weaknesses: The headline semantic results depend on an unvalidated evaluator. Appendix A omits ADE20K's actual vocabulary and relies on Llama 2 knowing its classes. The Cityscapes and ADE20K prompts also instruct the model to map stuff terms to background, despite these datasets containing annotated stuff categories. The exact-name override only partially mitigates this problem. Without audited mapping accuracy or comparisons against alternative mappings, the reliability of the reported mIoU remains uncertain.

Table 2's VOC comparison with ZeroSeg (41.6 versus 20.1 mIoU) changes both the segmentation pipeline and label-mapping procedure, without establishing a common evaluation protocol or accounting for pretrained segmentation supervision. Thus, the improvement cannot be attributed cleanly to BCC. No competing automatic-class method is evaluated on ADE20K or Cityscapes, leaving the state-of-the-art claims on those datasets insufficiently supported.

The separation between tuning and evaluation is unclear. Section 4.1 optimizes hyperparameters on VOC, while Table 2 uses each dataset's best caption-cycle count from Table 3. No disjoint tuning and evaluation subsets are identified, creating a risk of optimistic validation results. Repeated-run uncertainty is also absent despite stochastic clustering and caption generation.

The ablations do not adequately isolate the proposed contribution. Table 1's class-agnostic metric ignores category correctness, so it cannot establish improved semantic naming. Semantic mIoU against the plain-BLIP baseline, comparisons with repeated global or crop captions under equal decoding budgets, and ablations of alignment and denoising would distinguish the proposed design's benefits from simply generating more captions.

Several correctable implementation ambiguities hinder reproducibility: Equation 10 specifies independent maximum-IoU assignments rather than the stated Hungarian matching; alignment between the two spatial resolutions is unspecified; and the handling of concatenated positional channels before the frozen BLIP decoder is unclear. Runtime measurements are also missing despite using up to twenty captioning cycles in the main results.
